extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political and moral philosophy, theologians, and educated general readers interested in government, religion, and natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length critique and set of standards about what properly counts as philosophy, natural and moral explanation, and errors introduced by scholastic/Aristotelian traditions and corrupted religious practices. It lays out requirements for legitimate philosophical, scientific, and political reasoning and condemns various bad methods and doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy is 'the Knowledge acquired by Reasoning, from the Manner of the Generation of any thing, to the Properties; or from the Properties, to some possible Way of Generation of the same; to the end to bee able to produce, as far as matter, and humane force permit, such Effects, as humane life requireth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the Geometrician reasons from construction to properties and back to methods of construction; the Astronomer reasons from motions of sun and stars to causes of day, night, and seasons, enabling measurement of time. Philosophy is thus knowledge obtained by causal, rational inference aimed at practical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence is not Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prudence (original knowledge called Experience) is not a part of philosophy because it is not attained by reasoning but is a memory of past successions of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience/prudence is fallible: omission of small circumstances can frustrate expectation. Philosophy yields general, eternal, immutable truth; prudence (experience) does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Conclusions Are Not Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: False doctrine or false conclusions are not to be counted as philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one reasons aright in words he understands, he cannot conclude an error; so genuine philosophy excludes demonstrable falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural Revelation Is Not Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge known by supernatural revelation is not philosophy because it is not acquired by reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revelation belongs to a different epistemic category (faith/prophecy), not to rational causal inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority-based Learning Is Not Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning taken upon the credit of authors (reasoning from authority) is not philosophy; it is faith rather than reasoning from cause to effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge derived solely from texts or authors without causal reasoning should be treated as faith, not philosophical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for the Rise of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy requires leisure and stable commonwealths: 'Leasure is the mother of Philosophy; and Common-wealth, the mother of Peace, and Leasure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy arises where people have time away from provisioning and defending themselves; flourishing cities and political stability foster philosophical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Foundation for Natural Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy that lacks geometric/mathematical foundation is untrustworthy: geometry is the mother of natural science and necessary to understand motion and proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plato forbade entry to his school to those not versed in geometry. True natural philosophy must be built upon demonstrable mathematical truths; otherwise it becomes 'a Dream' set in 'senselesse and insignificant Language.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Philosophy Requires Civil Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral philosophy that attempts to define good and evil by private taste is inadequate; without civil government there is no general rule of good and evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a commonwealth the law (the will of the state) is the measure of good and evil, not individual appetites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic Must Be a Method, Not Wordplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Logic ('Logique') should be a true method of reasoning, not merely captious manipulations of words that puzzle others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scholastic verbal captations and equivocation; reasoning must proceed from properly defined concepts and causal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Conflating School Divinity with Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: University/philosophy that functions as a handmaid to religion and depends only on Aristotle ('Aristotelity') is not true philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When study is limited to authority and scholastic commentaries rather than causal reasoning, it degenerates into mere Aristotelianism, not philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject Separated (Abstract) Essences and Incorporeal Substantial Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of abstract essences or substantial forms (separated from bodies) is false and leads to absurdities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words like 'entity', 'essence', 'substantial form' are not names of things but signs of inferential relations. Positing incorporeal essences produces nonsensical claims (e.g., a soul being 'all of it' in every part of the body).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Wary of Obscure Metaphysical Distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions such as 'definitive' vs 'circumscriptive' place for incorporeal forms are meaningless jargon used to conceal vanity and insoluble problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accepting technical scholastic distinctions that have no clear referent or that serve only to rescue incoherent metaphysical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Intelligibility-violating Conceptions (e.g., Nunc-stans on Eternity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of concepts (such as Eternity as 'the Standing still of the Present Time' or Nunc-stans) that are unintelligible should be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical definitions must be comprehensible and not introduce paradoxes that obscure causal understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect Common-sense Constraints on Place and Quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that one body can be in many places at once, or many bodies in one place, are incongruent and absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphysical theorizing must respect the logical implications of extension, place, and quantity; avoid doctrines that deny ordinary spatial relations without explanatory account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Tautological/Circular Explanations in Natural Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations that define a cause by restating the effect (e.g., 'heaviness' causing descent by defining heaviness as an 'endeavour to go to the center') are vacuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural philosophy must provide explanatory mechanisms rather than merely renaming phenomena; do not accept circular definitions as causal accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the Idea of Quantity Being Added to a Pre-existing Body
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholastic notion that a body's apparent change in size is due to 'condensation' or 'rarefaction' understood as putting more or less quantity into a pre-existing body is incoherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantity is a determination of matter; philosophical accounts of change in size must coherently account for what 'quantity' means rather than treating it as something externally poured in or out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject Metaphors like 'Pouring In' Souls as Explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Saying the soul is 'created by pouring it in' (Creatur Infundendo) is a metaphorical, insufficient account of the soul's cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid explanatory metaphors that do not specify mechanisms or conditions; demand clearer causal accounts for the origin and operation of life/soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Explanations by Ubiquity of Species (Apparitions) for Sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining sense by an ubiquity of species or apparitions (visible species causing sight, audible species causing hearing) is an occult-style explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senses should be explained by intelligible mechanisms, not by invoking mysterious 'species' whose operations are left obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Explain Will by Will (Avoid Tautology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining volition by invoking a general 'faculty' (voluntas) that makes particular acts of will produces a circular explanation where the power is named as the cause of its act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical accounts of volition must avoid circular definitions and seek antecedent conditions or mechanisms that ground particular actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Use 'Ignorance' or 'Occult Qualities' as Explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributing events to 'Fortune', 'Occult Qualities', 'Sympathy', 'Antipathy', or other unknown qualities is substituting ignorance for explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good natural philosophy should avoid placeholders for unknown causes; instead investigate and specify causes and operations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Resolving Conclusions Before Establishing Premises
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophers who 'resolve of their Conclusions, before they know their Premises' commit an error that leads to absurdities in moral and civil philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reasoning proceeds from established premises; do not presuppose outcomes or import theological/authoritative assumptions that invert the reasoning process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure Public Good by the Law, Not Private Appetite
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commonwealth the law (the will and appetite of the State) is the measure of good and evil, not the private appetites of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging actions by private liking leads to subversion of the commonwealth; public ethics must take account of civil law and sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the Claim that Lawful Marriage Is Unchastity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is false philosophy to claim marriage is repugnant to chastity or continence; making lawful married use of wives a matter of vice is a mistaken moral doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition of priestly marriage is historically and politically motivated rather than founded on sound moral/philosophical grounds; evaluate such prohibitions skeptically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Equate Non-popular Government with Tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling all governments but the popular one 'tyranny' (and labeling kings 'tyrants') is a prejudice derived from Aristotelian political vocabulary and the passions of crowds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political terminology should not be used to express mere hatred or disapproval; recognize that different forms of government may be appropriate and that stability and law matter more than labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws Alone Do Not Govern Independently of Men
rubrics_metrics.description: The Aristotelian error is to suppose that in a well-ordered commonwealth not men, but laws should govern; this is a mistaken abstraction from how governance actually operates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that laws require men (and their power) to be enacted and enforced; political theory must account for human agents and institutions, not treat laws as self-acting entities.
